iti62:2.1: Found at [dn33:1.10.111]() and [sn48.23:1.3](), this went on to become a standard Abhidhamma set. The exact meaning is not immediately obvious. The verses here offer our best clues, so I annotate them closely.
iti62:2.3: The key term is _aññā_ (“enlightenment”), which is used throughout the Suttas to indicate the realization of arahantship specifically. For this reason I am not convinced by the commentarial explanation, which takes it as the knowledge arising first in a stream-enterer. | “The faculty of understanding that one’s enlightenment is imminent” is literally, “The faculty aware that ‘I shall know the unknown’”.
iti62:3.1: The three verses seem to correlate one-by-one to the three faculties. This first line indicates that the first faculty is restricted to those who have entered the noble path. The commentary takes this as meaning *all* those who have entered the noble path, but I think it is a subset.
iti62:3.3: In the Suttas, this is normally the “knowledge of the ending of defilements”, which is characteristic of the arahant (eg. [sn12.23]()).
iti62:3.4: “Without delay” means “in this very life”. | Ending of defilements without delay is taught numerous time as the advanced meditation practice aimed squarely at arahantship in this very life, typically explained as seeing the impermanence of the five aggregates ([sn22.55:10.1](), [sn22.81:5.1](), [an5.170](), [an6.27](), [an6.28]()).
iti62:4.4: This verse shows that the second faculty is the occasion when arahantship is realized.
iti62:5.4: The final faculty is the arahant living out their last life in peace.
